feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=-x+4{y}^{2},\,y(0.5)=0
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(1).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ starting from $x=0.5,$ we use a step size

$$
Δx=1-0.5=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δx$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-x+4{y}^{2})+(-{x}_{\text{new}}+4({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}))\cdot 0.5 \\  & =-0.25x-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}+{y}^{2}+({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =y-0.25x-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}+{y}^{2}+({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+{y}^{2}+y-0.25x-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+{y}^{2}+y-0.25x-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in this step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0.5+0.5=1.
$$

Then, the function $g$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+0+0-0.25(0.5)-0.25(1) \\  & =({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}-0.375.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y(0.5)=0$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})}{{g}^{′}(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})}.
$$

The derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=2{y}_{\text{new}}-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}^{\,2}-({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-0.375}{2({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-1}.
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $({y}_{\text{new}})_{1}=y(0.5)=0,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =0 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈-0.375 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈-0.29464 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈-0.29058 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{5} & ≈-0.29057\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that
$y(1)≈-0.29,$
rounded to two decimal places.
